rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in the gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Large electronegativity difference and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the ionicity gap ladder.
Polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise the valence band and shrink gaps across the largest anion population.
Partially filled d bands add states near the Fermi level and narrow gaps, but many d0 oxides are exceptions, so the penalty is mild.

skills.hypothesis: Domain proposal ordering candidates by cation-anion electronegativity difference: reward ionic halides and oxides, penalize polarizable chalcogenides, mildly penalize d-band metals. Fails for d0/d10 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated measurements.

rules.rationale: Halides carried the most negative source refractive-index effect; low polarizability inverts to wide gaps through the Moss relation.
Reverses the lowest-confidence source relation: d0/d10 transition-metal oxides are classic wide-gap ionic insulators, not narrow-gap metals.
Chalcogen-dominated compositions raised source refractive index; polarizable p-states imply small experimental gaps under Moss inversion.
Very heavy mean-Z increased source index; diffuse relativistic orbitals broaden bands and reduce measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Source-grounded counter-hypothesis: invert dielectric effects (halide, chalcogen, heavy-Z) while reversing the near-zero-confidence transition-metal penalty toward wide-gap d0 oxides. Fails if index and gap co-vary positively or if inversion misreads weak source signals.

lesson: Across two independent development generations the ionicity ladder led on mean AUC (72.7 vs 65.3, then 81.3 vs 73.5) with comparable final-best, so domain electronegativity ordering remains the safer frozen choice given source per-field confidences of only 0.006-0.30. Weak seeds appeared for both skills, indicating task variance rather than a specific rule defect, so I only softened the broad transition-metal penalty that conflicts with wide-gap d0 oxides instead of restructuring the skill.
revision_summary: Deployed skill v3 keeps the winning ionicity ladder, slightly strengthens the closed-shell halide interaction, deepens the chalcogenide penalty, and reduces the blanket transition-metal penalty from -0.30 to -0.22 because d0 oxides are wide-gap counterexamples; semantic mass end was trimmed to hand more late mass to the target-only anchor. The alternative is rebuilt as a sharper counter-hypothesis that keeps Moss-inverted source evidence (halide, chalcogen-dominant, very-high mean-Z) but explicitly reverses the lowest-confidence transition-metal relation via a d0-oxide interaction and switches the polarizability penalty from anion_family to the dominant_family chalcogen axis for diversity. All conditions map catalog fields to exact catalog values, each skill uses four rules, and all parameters lie inside the allowed ranges; feedback informed only relative ranking, not causal claims.
